Elliptical orbits are not preferred per se. Each satellite has their own needs. The article mentioned these satellites were going for a circular orbit but the insertion was botched and elliptical orbits are much easier to achieve than circular orbits - a circular orbit after all is just an extremely precise case of an elliptical orbit! Elliptical orbits mean the satellite spends a disproportonate amount of time over certain parts of the planet in a biased fashion. Circular orbits have a regular periodicity over any point on the planet. This actually also brings up an interesting special case of circular orbits. GSO or geostationary orbits are orbits where the satellite matches its orbital velocity exactly to earth's rotational velocity. In other words the satellite is constantly over exactly one spot on earth with countless uses from localized telecommunications to nonstop data collection on a certain point.
